stem:
Aisha's cousin has asthma, a non-communicable disease. The doctor links flare-up risk to air quality, activity plans, and asks for regular checkups and ongoing care rather than one short course of medicine alone.

Which approach is correct?

options.text: Continuous care, regular checkups, and attention to lifestyle and environment help manage the disease.
One short course of medicine gives permanent control, so no further care is needed.
Less physical activity always lowers every long-term health risk, so checkups can stop.
If the cousin looks well between flare-ups, regular checkups and care plans are unnecessary.

teacher.key_rationale: Non-communicable disease control needs ongoing care, checkups, and attention to lifestyle and environment. A one-time medicine course, stopping activity/checkups, or skipping care because someone looks well each miss that.
